title: Context and memory in an agent

items.stem: A teammate suggests putting all forty makerspace manuals into the context on every call, since the model's window is big enough to hold them. What is the strongest objection?

options.text: The model will refuse any context that holds more than one manual
Every call pays for all those tokens, and long contexts are used less well
The model forgets each manual as soon as it has read it once
The manuals would have to be rewritten before a model could read them

items.stem: Your program's setup (instructions and tool descriptions) is 1,000 tokens and the student's question is 100 tokens. In one run the model requests a tool, gets a 500-token result, requests a second tool, gets another 500-token result, and then writes its final answer. Each call re-sends the full history, and you ignore the model's own output. How many input tokens does the model read across the whole run?

On Monday the assistant tells Priya, by name, that she may use the laser cutter because she passed training. This is a brand-new conversation, and she did not mention training. What must the program have done?

options.text: Loaded her saved record into the context before the model was called
Relied on the model remembering her from its earlier conversations
Waited for the model to learn her status from its training
Kept the old conversation's context window open on its servers

items.stem: In an agent loop, why does each additional step cost more input tokens than the step before it?
Which information should the assistant fetch by retrieval at question time, rather than keep in the context all the time or save as a note?

options.text: The paragraph on aluminium cutting speeds, in a 300-page milling manual
The rule that the assistant must always cite the manual it used
The description of what the check_calendar tool does and takes
The fact that a given student has passed the router training
